source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (Digit Matrices)
finding: GPT-3 beat the average of UCLA undergraduates on a new text-only matrix task (Digit Matrices) built like Raven's SPM. Its error pattern looked human: harder with more rules, harder when spatially permuted.
numbers: Digit Matrices: humans N=40. Generative answers: GPT-3 vs humans OR=1.88, p=0.005, CI [1.21,2.91]. Multiple choice: OR=6.27, p=2.3e-8. Item-difficulty correlation GPT-3 vs humans r(30)=0.39, p=0.027.
limits: Text digits remove the visual part of Raven. Training-data leakage cannot be ruled out (acknowledged by authors). Later replications fail on altered versions (c03, c04, c05).
agent_relevance: Early sign that text-form Gf puzzles are solvable zero-shot, but only on familiar formats. A pass on a standard format is not proof of Gf.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (letter-string analogies)
finding: On letter-string analogies GPT-3 again beat humans overall, driven by zero-generalization items. Both humans and GPT-3 got worse as the number of required generalizations rose.
numbers: Letter-string humans N=57. GPT-3 vs humans OR=1.76, p=6.3e-5; zero-generalization items OR=1.76, p=0.0007. Effect of number of generalizations: GPT-3 OR=0.51, p=2e-16, CI [0.45,0.57].
limits: GPT-3 only; one alphabet.
agent_relevance: Difficulty rises with the number of stacked transformations. A code count of rules is a usable difficulty signal for the S0 gate.

source: Hodel and West (2023) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Rebuttal. Same letter-string tasks with a synthetic (shuffled) alphabet or larger letter interval: humans stay stable, GPT-3 collapses. Argues Webb's problems may be in training data.
numbers: GPT-3 generative accuracy on synthetic alphabet below 0.1 for extend-sequence, successor/predecessor and fix-alphabetic-sequence. Only remove-redundant and sort stayed near Webb's level. Comprehension checks: GPT-3 at least 30% of original level on all but one task.
limits: Mostly GPT-3 only; small human samples. Authors also say human tests may not measure LLMs validly.
agent_relevance: Good novelty probe: re-skin a familiar puzzle with a changed alphabet. A big drop means recall, not reasoning.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Counterfactual letter-string analogies (permuted alphabets, symbol alphabets). Human accuracy stayed flat across alphabets. GPT-3, 3.5 and 4 dropped with more permuted letters and dropped sharply on symbols. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were no better than GPT-3 on the original task.
numbers: Humans N=46 in replication (Webb humans N=57). Alternate-rule errors: GPT-3 5.81%, GPT-4 22%, GPT-3.5 38.59%; humans about 15% in the same category. GPT performance on original problems was below the human average, unlike in Webb.
limits: Own human group scored higher than Webb's group (pool or protocol). Chat tuning may have hurt.
agent_relevance: Surface re-encoding is a cheap way to separate rule inference from memory. Add a mutated-encoding check (G3) before trusting a Gf-style answer.

source: Stevenson, Pafford, van der Maas, Mitchell (2025) Can LLMs generalize analogy solving like children can?
finding: Children, adults and LLMs on letter-string analogies in Latin, Greek (near transfer) and symbol (far transfer) domains. Humans transferred; LLMs did not. Newer open models also scored lower on Greek and Symbol than Latin.
numbers: Paper cites earlier work: GPT models about 60% in Latin. Table 9: Gemma-2 27B and Llama-3.1 405B did better without message history on the Symbol alphabet; elsewhere history helped. Exact child N not copied.
limits: Letter strings are one narrow paradigm.
agent_relevance: Far transfer is the human advantage. The S0 gate should flag far-transfer problems as hard for the base model and spend search there.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks
finding: Across 11 tasks, GPT-4 and others do non-trivially on counterfactual variants (base-9 arithmetic, rotated grids) but always worse than on default versions, even with 0-shot chain of thought.
numbers: Parseable programs from GPT-3.5 fall from 99% (default) to 62%, 71%, 75% for vertically flipped, 90-degree and 180-degree rotated settings. Counterfactual comprehension checks show the model understood the new rules.
limits: Not Gf-specific. The counterfactual design is the useful part.
agent_relevance: The counterfactual-twin test is a ready S0 novelty detector: run default and altered form; a large gap means off the learned path.

source: Gendron, Bao, Witbrock, Dobbie (2023) Large Language Models Are Not Strong Abstract Reasoners
finding: Benchmark of abstract reasoning (ARC text, ACRE, RAVEN text/symbolic, PVR, BIG-Bench-F). LLMs score low. Chain of thought, code refinement and many-shot examples gave little help except for GPT-4 and text-davinci-003.
numbers: Open QA, GPT-4: ARC-text 0.119, RAVEN text 0.410, symbolic 0.330; text-davinci-003 RAVEN text 0.343; GPT-3.5-turbo 0.226. Multiple choice RAVEN (chance 0.125): GPT-4 text 0.697, symbolic 0.535; text-davinci-003 0.461 and 0.452. 16 examples raised BIG-Bench-F to about 0.6; PVR stayed near 0.26.
limits: Early models.
agent_relevance: Prompt tricks that help knowledge tasks do not help fresh abstraction. Do not assume chain of thought fixes novelty problems.

source: Moskvichev, Odouard, Mitchell (2023) The ConceptARC Benchmark
finding: 160 easier ARC-style tasks over 16 concepts, three tries per test input. Humans far above machines, including text GPT-4 zero-shot.
numbers: Humans 83-97% per concept (over 90% on 11 of 16). Kaggle first place never above 80%, below 60% on 11 of 16 (21% on original ARC). GPT-4 below 30% on 15 of 16 concepts (33% on one); Count 3%, Copy 7%. Gap humans vs first-place program about 40 points.
limits: Early text-only GPT-4; later models score far higher.
agent_relevance: Concept-group grading gives a map of which basic concepts fail (counting, copying). Useful for a skills-level S0 map.

source: Xu, Li, Vaezipoor, Sanner, Khalil (2024) LLMs and the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
finding: GPT-4 solves few ARC tasks when the grid is given as text. Failures tie to how objects are spread across the flattened text. An object-based description made by an external tool almost doubled the score; on the new 1D-ARC GPT-4 does much better.
numbers: GPT-4: 13/50 of the simplest ARC tasks with direct grid text, 23/50 with object representation. 1D-ARC object form, GPT-4 per task family out of 50: 50, 49, 37, 40, 50, 48, 49, 21, 20, 42, 37. Gains per family +4% to +96% (Move 3 Pixels +74%, Denoise +52%).
limits: 50 tasks per family, so each task is 2 points.
agent_relevance: Change the representation before adding reasoning. A code tool that lists objects, counts and colors belongs in front of the model for grid-like problems.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search: Inductive Reasoning with Language Models
finding: An agent-loop method: the model writes several abstract hypotheses in words, then Python programs for each; code runs them on the examples and survivors are applied to the test. Beat direct prompting on ARC.
numbers: 100-problem ARC subset (GPT-4): direct prompting 17%; programs from hypotheses 23%; with LLM-summarised hypotheses 30%; human picks from LLM hypotheses 33%; 33 of 49 selected hypotheses gave correct programs (67%). Without programs (language only) GPT-4 fell to 19%.
limits: Verification uses the given examples only, so the G3 risk of fitting the examples remains.
agent_relevance: Close to our induce, verify, apply loop. Explicit hypotheses plus code check beat plain answering.

source: Li et al. (2024) Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning
finding: Induction (write a program) and transduction (predict the output directly) solve different ARC tasks from the same training. Induction is better at precise computation and composing concepts; transduction at fuzzy perceptual concepts. Ensembling gets near average human.
numbers: Ensemble 56.75% on ARC-AGI-1 public eval, 'nearly as well as the average human'; later 61.9% with Akyurek's test-time training. Ensemble rule: try induction first, then transduction if no candidate program fits.
limits: Needs synthetic training data and test-time training.
agent_relevance: Two routes chosen by code: checkable route first, direct guess as fallback. Fits the S0 gate.

source: Akyurek et al. (2025) The Surprising Effectiveness of Test-Time Training for Few-Shot Learning
finding: Briefly updating weights on the task's own examples lifts ARC scores several-fold; also helps BIG-Bench Hard.
numbers: ARC (80 validation tasks, pass@2): fine-tuned 17.5%, with TTT 45.0% (+27.5 points); 53.0% with BARC base; ensemble with program synthesis 61.9% ('matching average human performance'). BBH 10-shot: 50.5% to 57.8% (+7.3).
limits: Needs weight updates, outside a no-training scaffold. Pass@2 not pass@1.
agent_relevance: In-context examples alone are not enough for novel tasks. A no-training analogue is voting in code over transformed views.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
finding: Reasoning models on I-RAVEN look strong but collapse on I-RAVEN-X (larger value ranges, perception noise). A neuro-symbolic abduction model degrades far less.
numbers: o3-mini (medium) 86.6% to 17.0% (chance 12.5%) with 3.4x more reasoning tokens; DeepSeek R1 80.6% to 23.2%; o3-mini high 92.6% on I-RAVEN. ARLC neuro-symbolic: 98.6% to 88.0%.
limits: Symbolic attributes given; perception simulated.
agent_relevance: A rule solver in code beat reasoning models once the problem left the usual range. For rule-structured Gf items, call code, not more thinking.

source: LeGris, Vong, Lake, Gureckis (2024) H-ARC: human performance on ARC
finding: Large human baseline on the full original ARC. Humans are good but not perfect, and almost every task is solvable by some person.
numbers: N=1,729 online participants, 800 tasks. Training set 76.2% (CI 73.3-77.2); public evaluation set 64.2% (CI 55.9-68.9). 790 of 800 tasks solved by at least one person within three attempts.
limits: Crowd workers; earlier estimates were higher.
agent_relevance: Human reference is about 64% on evaluation tasks, so a perfect score is not the human norm.

source: Chollet, Knoop, Kamradt, Landers, Pinkard (2026) ARC-AGI-2
finding: ARC-AGI-1 was saturating under test-time adaptation; the o3 preview scored high. On ARC-AGI-2 the same systems score near floor.
numbers: ARC-AGI-1: 20% (2020 top); about 34% (early 2024); ARC Prize 2024 top 55.5%, eligible winner 53.5%; o3 preview 76% (about $200/task) and 88% (about $20,000/task); o3-medium 53%. ARC-AGI-2 semi-private (May 2025): o3-mini high 3.0%, o3 medium 3.0%, ARChitects 2.5%, o4-mini 2.4%, Icecuber 1.6%, o1-pro low 0.9%, Claude 3.7 (8K) 0.9%. Below 5% there is little signal.
limits: Compute cost differs by orders of magnitude; semi-private set only.
agent_relevance: Track cost per task with accuracy. Stacked compositional rules, not just novelty, defeat current search.

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC-AGI-2: human testing
finding: First-party human testing of candidate ARC-AGI-2 tasks. Tasks need deliberate thought, unlike many ARC-AGI-1 tasks.
numbers: 407 participants, 515 sessions, 1,848 unique test pairs, 13,405 attempts, 8,277 solved (62%). Median time per attempted pair 2.3 min; average task completion 2.7 min. Every kept task solved by at least two independent non-experts. ARC-AGI-1 private tasks: two people scored 97% and 98%.
limits: Paid volunteers in a room; tasks pre-selected for solvability.
agent_relevance: Humans need minutes of deliberation, so time per task is a real cost for any scaffold claiming Gf.

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC Prize 2025 Technical Report
finding: 2025 competition: refinement loops (generate, test against feedback, improve) are the defining method. Top Kaggle score 24% on ARC-AGI-2.
numbers: 1,455 teams, 15,154 entries. NVARC 24.03% (about $0.20/task); ARChitects 16.53%; MindsAI 12.64%. Paper award: Tiny Recursive Model (7M parameters) about 8% on ARC-AGI-2, 45% on ARC-AGI-1. Gemini 3 Pro used 96 reasoning tokens on one ARC-AGI-1 task, Gemini 3 Deep Think 138,000.
limits: Kaggle compute limits; ARC Prize website lists ARChitects at 15.42%, report at 16.53%.
agent_relevance: Refinement against a feedback signal is the working pattern, matching G2 (revise only from real output).

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC Prize 2025 Technical Report: model refinement harnesses
finding: A scaffold (harness) around a commercial model, with no training, raised ARC-AGI-2. Poetiq's open-sourced harness on Gemini 3 Pro was verified by ARC Prize.
numbers: Gemini 3 Pro baseline 31% at $0.81/task; with refinement harness 54% at $31/task. Claude Opus 4.5 comparable accuracy at about $60/task (reported by Poetiq).
limits: Harness is domain-specific; cost rose about 38x for +23 points.
agent_relevance: Direct support for the thesis that a scaffold lifts novel-problem accuracy, at known cost. Budget caps needed.

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC Prize 2025 Technical Report: knowledge dependence
finding: Authors argue AI reasoning now works where the task is covered by pretraining knowledge and a verifiable feedback signal exists. Human reasoning is not bound to knowledge in the same way.
numbers: No single number; examples: ARC-AGI-2, IMO 2025 gold, ICPC 2025. They judge the accuracy gap is now engineering and the efficiency gap a science problem.
quote: Sufficient task knowledge coverage exists in the pretraining corpus.
limits: Opinion of benchmark authors.
agent_relevance: The S0 gate can ask two code-checkable questions: is there a verifier, and is the domain well covered? If neither, expect weak results and escalate.

source: Chollet et al. (2026) ARC Prize 2025: small purpose-built models
finding: Very small trained recurrent or compression models reached non-trivial ARC scores, so ARC can be partly solved by narrow methods.
numbers: TRM 7M parameters: 45% ARC-AGI-1, about 8% ARC-AGI-2. CompressARC 76K parameters: about 20% on ARC-AGI-1 evaluation, about 20 min per puzzle on one GPU.
limits: Trained on ARC-style data, so not zero-shot Gf.
agent_relevance: ARC scores alone do not prove general fluid reasoning; keep non-ARC probes in the S0 sort.

source: Gendron et al. (2023) fine-tuning versus prompting
finding: Fine-tuning a small model on RAVEN-style synthetic data makes it near perfect in-distribution, but it falls on new syntax and tasks.
numbers: Fine-tuned LLaMA2 on symbolic RAVEN-train reaches 96.5% on the text task; accuracy drops significantly on out-of-distribution tasks.
limits: Small models, synthetic data.
agent_relevance: Learning the format is not learning the skill. Run an out-of-distribution check after any adaptation.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) token cost
finding: Reasoning models spent more tokens on the harder variant and still failed, so effort was not the limit.
numbers: o3-mini (medium) used 2.7x more reasoning tokens on the harder variant and fell to 17.0%; R1 22.8% in one condition; chance 12.5%; neuro-symbolic best 88.0%.
limits: One task family.
agent_relevance: More thinking tokens do not fix a rule the model cannot represent. Cap tokens and switch method at an impasse.

source: Akyurek et al. (2025) voting design
finding: Test-time training works with augmented views of the task and hierarchical voting over them; the 61.9% result added program synthesis as a second route.
numbers: Hierarchical voting beat flattened voting; fine-tuned 18.3% to 47.1% with TTT in one table; BARC base 53.0% with TTT; ensemble 61.9%.
limits: Gains need TTT; voting alone not isolated.
agent_relevance: Vote in code across transformed views (rotate, flip, recolor); a no-training analogue.

source: Cattell (1943) and Horn and Cattell (1967): fluid and crystallised intelligence
finding: Original definition of Gf as reasoning on novel material, measured by Raven-type matrices, series completion and classification. Not opened this session; listed so ARC-style tasks link back to the psychometric roots.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened; use primary sources before quoting.
agent_relevance: Defines the S0 sort: Gf-type (novel) versus Gc-type (learned knowledge) problems.

source: Chollet (2019) On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC origin)
finding: Defines intelligence as skill-acquisition efficiency and introduces ARC with core-knowledge priors. Paper not opened; content taken from citing papers.
numbers: Not read; ARC-AGI-1 has 400 training and 400 evaluation tasks plus private sets (from the ARC-AGI-2 paper).
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Intelligence as efficiency under novelty: report accuracy together with cost and examples used.
